content: Acetaminophen, aspirin, and salicylamide are medications approved by the FDA for the temporary relief of pain caused by headaches, muscle aches, colds, and flu, as well as for the reduction of fever. Adults are advised to take two caplets every six hours, with a maximum of eight caplets in a 24-hour period. For children under 12 years of age, a doctor should be consulted before use. This product contains acetaminophen, which carries a risk of severe liver damage if taken in excess. Specifically, liver damage may occur if more than eight tablets are consumed within 24 hours, if the medication is taken alongside other drugs containing acetaminophen, or if the individual consumes three or more alcoholic drinks daily while using this product. It is important not to use this medication with any other product containing acetaminophen, as this could result in an overdose and lead to serious health complications. Additionally, the medication should not be used for more than 10 days to treat pain or for more than three days to treat fever unless directed by a healthcare provider. Patients should discontinue use and seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve, if pain or fever persists or worsens, if new symptoms develop, or if redness or swelling is present. There is limited information available regarding the use of this medication in pediatric, geriatric, pregnant, or nursing populations, as well as in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no specific guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, or immunocompromised patients. The medication is administered orally, and there is no information provided about its compatibility with intravenous administration. In the event of a suspected overdose, individuals should immediately contact the National Poison Help hotline at 1-800-222-1222. The pharmacological details, including the mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of this medication, are not well-documented. Additionally, there is no detailed information available regarding its clinical studies, storage conditions, or packaging. Patients should be cautious about consuming alcohol while taking this medication, as the interaction between alcohol and acetaminophen, aspirin, and salicylamide has not been fully established. It is recommended to consult a healthcare provider regarding the potential effects of alcohol consumption in combination with this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name ZEE PAIN AID®.
